findings.what_viewer_sees: On 'trying', the toppling pile slides off down-left and accelerates to about 130-180 px/frame. The Bacon print then stops dead with a ~250x220 px corner still in the lower-left of frame and hangs there motionless for 4 frames before the hard cut to Forster. It reads as the paper snagging on the frame edge.
findings.evidence: Exact keyframe-anchored frames F3236-F3247 (review6/grab_s2/x_03236_12x1_w480.jpg): the print moves from F3240 to F3241, F3241-F3244 are identical, and F3245 is the Forster portrait. Detector E10 motion_stop at F3242 (motion 10.55 -> 0.08). Computed print corners at tp=1 are (425,860), (540,1274), (299,1341), (184,927), so part of the print is still in frame.
findings.likely_cause: tp = prog(tt, t.tryW-0.05, t.tryW+0.7, E.in) clamps to 1 at 108.02 s, but the shot runs on to t.s018-0.07 = 108.15 s. At tp=1 the rotated, translated print has not left the frame yet. Because E.in is cubic, the print is at peak speed at the moment it clamps.
findings.code_location: engine/www/ep/ep01/ch1.js:783 (the same tp also drives the stack at :791)
findings.suggested_fix: Do not clamp the fall: `const u = Math.max(0, (tt - (t.tryW - 0.05)) / 0.75), tp = u * u * u;`. The print keeps accelerating and is fully out of frame by F3243 (e.g. corner at (-266,988)). The stack uses the same tp but is already off-screen, so nothing else changes.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 'whip to Kanyakumari' does not whip. The camera starts from rest under a 6-frame horizontal ghost smear and swings for ~0.35 s (peak F3518). It comes to a complete stop at F3523-F3525, sets off again on a second push (peak F3541) and stops again before the cut to the flood page. The result is a settle-and-go hiccup inside a 1.5 s shot. Because the camera is nearly still while the smear is applied, the smear reads as ghosting rather than motion blur.
findings.evidence: Frame-to-frame mean absolute difference from an exact decode: F3513 1.7, F3518 4.04, F3523-F3525 0.06-0.12, F3541 2.77, F3555 0.27. Detector E14 motion_stop at F3522. Exact tile x_03508_12x1_w480.jpg shows F3512 is the first India frame, which matches the encoder keyframe at 117.0667 s.
findings.likely_cause: camAt eases each key segment with the DESTINATION key's ease (b.ease). The E.outExpo placed on keys[0] is therefore never used. Both segments (0-0.35 s and 0.35-1.47 s) get the default cubic E.inOut, so velocity is zero at the cut, at the 0.35 s key and at the end.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one segment that whips in and settles: `keys: [{ t: 0, lat: 7.2, lon: 77.9, alt: 0.24, tilt: 55, heading: 8 }, { t: t.s019 - WHIP, lat: 8.8, lon: 77.3, alt: 0.21, tilt: 58, heading: -2, ease: E.outExpo }]`. The camera is then fastest at the cut, where the smear is, and decays continuously with no stop. The same ignored first-key ease appears at ch1.js:411, 426, 443 and 537, all in S1's range.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The 3D explorer (about 430 px tall) breaks into a full-cadence run, one stride every ~0.2 s, but hardly travels. For the first ~0.45 s his body stays in place while the legs complete 1.5 strides. He moves at a believable pace only around F3675-F3685, then slows to a near-standstill while still running before the wave hits. The planted foot visibly skates backwards on the planet (treadmill/moonwalk).
findings.evidence: Exact full-res crops F3656-F3673 (x_03656_18x1_w320_c450-330-1050-930.jpg): the torso stays fixed while the legs cycle. Body centroid track at full res: 723->765 px over F3657-F3670 (~3 px/frame), ~15-20 px/frame at F3671-F3683, ~3-5 px/frame at F3695-F3704. The run clip is active from F3654 until HitRecieve at F3704.
findings.likely_cause: Root motion and clip speed are unrelated. ch1.js:856 moves the hero along the planet with cubic E.inOut (zero speed at both ends) over only 0.25 rad (~0.75 units, ~320 px) in 1.68 s. Meanwhile ch1.js:307 plays Run_Right at full speed for the whole span. Ground speed therefore never matches stride speed: ~0.2 units/s at the ends and ~1.3 units/s at the peak.
findings.suggested_fix: Drive `be` close to linearly over a longer arc, e.g. `lerp(-0.35, 0.2, prog(tt, G2 + 0.35, t.carved - 0.05, E.lin))`, keeping the -0.05 pushback; the end point is unchanged, so the wave hit stays in sync. Slow the cycle to the new ground speed with Actor.play's speed option: `.play(G2 + 0.35, clip('Run_Right', 'Run'), { fade: 0.15, speed: 0.55 })`. Tune the speed until the planted foot holds still for 2-3 frames.

findings.what_viewer_sees: After the wave soaks the explorer it recedes up-right. At F3731 its whole back slope, a bright cyan band spanning roughly x 1230-1920 and y 420-900, is still on screen. At F3732 it is simply gone: a large element vanishes in one frame while moving at ~40 px/frame.
findings.evidence: Exact tile x_03708_30x1_w480.jpg (F3708-F3737): the wave tail is present through F3731 and absent from F3732. Detector E17 motion_stop at F3733 is this vanish.
findings.likely_cause: wp() = prog(tt, t.carved-1.25, t.carved+0.85, E.lin) clamps at 1, and the wave is drawn only while p < 1. At p=1 the wave anchor is at x≈2028, but the 945-px-long body trails back to x≈1165, so about half the wave is still in frame when it is dropped.
findings.suggested_fix: Let the wave travel until it has fully left the frame: `const wp = (tt) => (tt - (t.carved - 1.25)) / 2.1;` and draw while `p > 0 && p < 1.45`. p=1.45 is reached at 125.3 s, before the 126.28 s cut, and at that point every part of the wave is at x>1920. The speed is unchanged; only the clamp goes.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the soaked close-up, each water bead drips from the explorer's beard, falls ~70 px in front of his dark shirt, then disappears in one frame mid-air at chest height. The next bead pops in at 40% size under the beard. This repeats every 1.6 s, three times in the shot.
findings.evidence: Exact head crops F3836-F3882, every 2nd frame (x_03836_24x2_w240_c880-220-1180-620.jpg): the bead grows F3838-F3866, falls F3868-F3878 and is gone at F3880. Per the code it vanishes at 127.70, 129.30 and 130.90 s.
findings.likely_cause: beadAt hides the bead with `bead.visible = fall < 0.75`, i.e. mid-fall, and restarts the next one at scale 0.4.
findings.suggested_fix: Shrink the bead out instead of hiding it, e.g. `bead.visible = fall < 1; bead.scale.setScalar((0.15 + 0.85 * Math.min(1, ph / 0.45)) * (1 - clamp((fall - 0.55) / 0.45)));`. Alternatively, extend the fall so the bead drops out of the bottom of the frame.

findings.what_viewer_sees: For 'All their points turned towards the south', a 1500x104 dark quote bar appears at full opacity in a single frame across the top of the map (F4387), while the KAMCHATKA pill beside it fades over 6 frames. For the remaining 3.3 s of the shot the bar covers Greenland's southern tip (Cape Farewell) and the upper half of Kamchatka. Two of the five tips just listed are hidden exactly while the quote says all their points turned south.
findings.evidence: Exact top-strip tile x_04380_12x1_w640_c0-0-1920-400.jpg (F4380-F4391): Greenland's red fill and the top band darken between F4386 and F4387 with no ramp. Full frame x_04440_1x1_w1920.jpg shows the bar over Greenland, with only a sliver visible above it, and over the top of Kamchatka. Detector E24 pop at F4387.
findings.likely_cause: The bar's alpha `a = 1 - prog(tt, t.s022 - 0.4, t.s022 - 0.1)` has a fade-out but no fade-in. The bar is also placed at y 60-164, which is exactly where the s003 match-cut framing puts Greenland and Kamchatka.
findings.suggested_fix: Fade the bar in: `const a = prog(tt, t.quote21 - 0.1, t.quote21 + 0.15, E.out) * (1 - prog(tt, t.s022 - 0.4, t.s022 - 0.1));`. Move it to the bottom band over Antarctica: `F.round(ctx, 210, 950, 1500, 104, 20)`, text y 136 -> 1026, cursor rect y 86 -> 976. South America's tip ends near y 913, so the 950-1054 band covers only Antarctica.

findings.what_viewer_sees: The magnifier has no entrance or exit. It pops in at full size at F4774, four frames after the punch-in cut at F4770, and sits still for two frames before gliding. At the end, 17 frames into the static wide framing that starts at F4839, the ~165 px lens and its handle vanish from the map card in one frame (F4856).
findings.evidence: Exact tiles x_04768_18x1_w480.jpg (F4768-F4785) and x_04836_24x1_w480.jpg (F4836-F4859). Detector E30 pop at F4856 (block diff 44.3 vs local median 1.1).
findings.likely_cause: The magnifier is gated by `tt > t.staring - 0.5 && tt < t.s023 + 0.5` with no alpha or scale envelope. Its start is 0.1 s after the CAMS framing cut at t.staring - 0.6, and its end is a hard cutoff in the middle of the s023 wide shot.
findings.suggested_fix: Start it on the cut frame and give it an envelope: `const ma = env(tt, t.staring - 0.6, t.s023 + 0.5, 0.15, 0.3); if (ma > 0) { ctx.save(); ctx.globalAlpha *= ma; X.magnifier(...); ctx.restore(); }`. Alternatively, end it at t.s023 - 0.07 so it leaves on the cut.

findings.what_viewer_sees: In the byline close-up ('Hold on to him. He matters more than you'd think'), the yellow ring drawn around the blurred byline runs along the baseline of the title above it and paints over the bottoms of the letters. From F4995 until the cut, the headline reads 'THE DRTP. REVISITED': the I loses its bottom serif and becomes a T, and the comma becomes a period. It is the largest text on screen for ~2.8 s and looks like a typo.
findings.evidence: Exact crops x_04989_12x1_w320_c880-380-1380-620.jpg: F4989-F4994 read 'DRIP,', and F4995-F5000 read 'DRTP.' as the ring's top arc crosses the glyph bottoms. Full-res crop x_05030_1x1_w1200_c900-100-1900-600.jpg shows the same. It is visible even in sheet_09 at 2:47.00-2:49.00.
findings.likely_cause: `ctx.ellipse(220, 200, 200, 52, ...)` puts the ring's top at y≈148, and its 7 px stroke covers y 144.5-151.5. The title is drawn at y=150 on an alphabetic baseline (ch1.js:992; fx.js text uses textBaseline 'alphabetic'), and the ring is drawn after the title, so it covers the glyph bottoms.
findings.suggested_fix: Fit the ring to the byline bars only (y 182-214), e.g. `ctx.ellipse(220, 206, 205, 38, -0.04, ...)`. Its top stroke edge then sits at ≈164.5, below the comma's descender. Alternatively, draw the ring before the title text.

result.intended_notes:
Intended and reading well: the hard cuts on narration beats (E1, E4, E5, E11, E13 as a cut, E15, E16, E18, E20-E23, E25, E33, E34), each landing on its segment start or word. The 1973/1976 desk 'virtual camera' punch-ins (E26-E29, E31, E32). Designed slams and pops: the JUICE CHECK stamp slam and shake (E2/E3), the Bacon page zipping into the corner (E6, inOutExpo, ~7 frames), the three archival pages dropping onto the stack (E7-E9), the wax seal and refund deflate (E19), sheet slide-ins, Humboldt triangle pops, the headline typing with strike and 'P' overtype, and the Gondwana watermark flicker at 'think' (168.09-168.64 s, a deliberate subliminal cue). Mapping of the remaining events: E10 = S2-1, E14 = S2-2, E17 = S2-4, E24 = S2-6, E30 = S2-7.

Chunk seams at F2700, 3150, 3600, 4050, 4500 and 4950 show no look change. Each seam-pair difference matches its neighbours: median block difference is +0.2-0.3 (keyframe noise) and mean colour shift is ≤0.4 levels. F2700 falls in the middle of the stamp slam and is consistent with it.

Clean when stepped at full rate: s015-s016 drift, stamp and rewind (85.9-94.3 s); flat-map punch-in, triangles and ≈ (94.4-99.3 s); the s017 '?' grow and page drops; the Forster and Humboldt Ken Burns moves (smooth, no clamp kinks); page underlines; Patagonia; the list-pill crossfades; the typing desk; the s024 drip arrows and cutaway drill; and the ch1->ch2 cut at F5260. Narration sync is good throughout; no visual is more than 0.4 s off its word.

Not reported:
- The Humboldt globe has the same settle-then-push from per-key easing (stopped F4131-F4137, keys at ch1.js:911), but its second move is small.
- The stamp shake translates only the 2D overlay, not the globe; this is imperceptible over its 6 frames.
- The ignored keys[0] ease behind S2-2 also appears at ch1.js:411, 426, 443 and 537, which belong to S1.

Tooling warning: grab.py labels can be one frame late. Its -ss seek with cfr jpg output duplicates the first decoded frame at some seek points; near 117 s, its 'f3513' is true F3512, confirmed by the encoder keyframe at the cut, 117.0667 s. All frame numbers here come from keyframe-anchored passthrough decoding (scratchpad/review6/s2tools/xgrab.py) and agree with the README's event frames.
